hypotheses.note: AffineSubspace ℝ E, E a bare real vector space

hypotheses.paper: S ∩ W non vide et saturé pour F_W
hypotheses.note: ((S:Set E) ∩ W).Nonempty ∧ (A ∈ S∩W → FW W A B → B ∈ S∩W)

findings: l.195: « L'espace tout entier est une variété d'appui » holds exactly when W ≠ ∅ (isVarieteAppui_top_iff); W = ∅ is the degenerate case the paper plainly excludes, so not reported as imprecise.
questions: l.187–188: « cette définition équivaut à celle de Bourbaki, EVT chap. II p. 83 ». Bourbaki is not in the hub; we took his definition to be: S ∩ W ≠ ∅, and every open segment ]x, y[ with x, y ∈ W that meets S has x, y ∈ S. The equivalence is proved (isVarieteAppui_iff_openSegment, W convex). The author should confirm that this is Bourbaki's wording.

hypotheses.paper: W un convexe dont le support E est de dimension finie
hypotheses.note: Convex ℝ W, FiniteDimensional ℝ (affineSpan ℝ W).direction; the _of_finiteDimensional form needs only affineSpan (L ∩ W) finite-dimensional (weakened), and also gives affineSpan F = affineSpan (L ∩ W)

labels.label: bzrem:c3s1r2_support_interieur_fermeture

hypotheses.paper: (1°) W convexe de support E de dimension finie (context of Prop. 5)
hypotheses.note: FiniteDimensional ℝ (affineSpan ℝ W).direction and W.Nonempty; « son intérieur » = intrinsicInterior ℝ W
any Hausdorff topological vector space structure on the ambient space. Its trace on the finite-dimensional support is the canonical topology

hypotheses.paper: (2°) W convexe compact de dimension finie
hypotheses.note: IsCompact W and finite-dimensional support; inter_eq_closure_facette needs only IsClosed W (weakened)

questions: l.222: 1° is read in Prop. 5's context, so W ≠ ∅ (a variété d'appui exists only then; for W = ∅ there is no facette). Hypothesis W.Nonempty.
l.225: « la fermeture compacte E de F » is a [sic] in the transcription, read F̄, the closure of the facette F of Prop. 5. Proved for every facette F with S ∩ W = L ∩ W, together with: F̄ is compact.

l.223: the paper's ambient space has no topology; « intérieur », « compact » and « fermeture » refer to the canonical topology of the finite-dimensional support. We formalized them on an ambient Hausdorff TVS. Every real vector space carries such a structure, and its trace on a finite-dimensional subspace is the canonical one.

hypotheses.note: alphaW_inter_iff needs no non-emptiness; alphaW_induit carries the read hypothesis

questions: l.233: « α(W′) est induite par α(W) » read as: for A, B ∈ W ∩ L, A α(W′) B ↔ A α(W) B (alphaW_inter_iff states it as AlphaW (W ∩ L) A B ↔ A ∈ L ∧ B ∈ L ∧ AlphaW W A B).

instance.statement: in the closed square [0,1]² (Benzecri.square = Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1 ⊂ ℝ×ℝ) the line y = 0 is a variété d'appui and the diagonal y = x is not
instance.extra: Benzecri.antidiag_appui_not_support: the anti-diagonal x + y = 0 is a variété d'appui of [0,1]² and the support of no facette. This is the commentary's « la réciproque n'est pas vraie » in finite dimension (l.195–197).

kb_proposals: Chapter3/Appui: Prop. 5 does not need the paper's « point interne ». Take a point of L ∩ W whose facette has a support of maximal finrank (Nat.sSup_mem on a bounded set). The midpoint trick and eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq then show that this support contains L ∩ W.

Chapter3/Appui: in finite dimension a facette F is the intrinsicInterior of W when its support is that of W (remarque_facette_interieur). To feed interieur_of_fw, get a finite family in F from exists_affineIndependent, with finiteness from finite_set_of_fin_dim_affineIndependent applied in the affine space ↥(affineSpan ℝ F).

Chapter3/Appui: for A ∈ F and P ∈ affineSpan F ∩ W, the half-open segment [A, P) lies in F. Use ε = 1 − t in alphaW_iff_extend. This gives F̄ ⊇ S ∩ W with no closure-of-intrinsic-interior lemma, which mathlib lacks at this pin.
